title: Varun Chakravarthy Ruled Out of Afghanistan T20Is With Side Strain
excerpt: Scans revealed the side strain after Sunday's opener in Delhi; Ravi Bishnoi comes into the XI and Chakaravarthy's Asian Games availability is now in doubt.
body:
• Mystery spinner Varun Chakaravarthy has been ruled out of the remaining two T20Is against Afghanistan after scans revealed a side strain suffered during the series opener in Delhi on Sunday.
  • The BCCI confirmed Chakaravarthy felt "sudden-onset discomfort in his left lateral abdominal region" while bowling his third over; Ravi Bishnoi replaced him in the XI for Tuesday's second T20I.
  • The injury is a fresh blow to a comeback: Chakaravarthy had only just returned to the national side after a hamstring injury on the England tour and a rehab stint at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru.
  • His availability for the Asian Games in Japan — the team leaves on September 18 — is now in doubt, and the latest setback has put the CoE's fitness management under renewed scrutiny.

India's mystery spinner Varun Chakaravarthy has been ruled out of the remaining two T20Is against Afghanistan after scans confirmed a side strain, cutting short a comeback that had lasted exactly one match.

The 35-year-old featured in the series opener at the Arun Jaitley Stadium on Sunday, bowling an economical 1 for 16 in his four overs as India won by seven wickets. But the BCCI confirmed on Monday that he had picked up a fresh injury during the game. "Varun Chakaravarthy experienced sudden-onset discomfort in his left lateral abdominal region while bowling his third over in the first T20I," the board said in a statement. "Scans have revealed a side strain, and he has subsequently been ruled out of the remaining two T20Is. Bishnoi replaces injured Varun."

Captain Shreyas Iyer confirmed the change at the toss for the second T20I on Tuesday: "Varun is injured and Ravi Bishnoi comes in." India made one change to the playing XI, with Afghanistan fielding an unchanged side.

A comeback cut short

The timing is cruel. Chakaravarthy had only recently returned to the national squad after recovering from a hamstring injury suffered on India's tour of England in July — an injury that had forced him to miss the T20I tour of Zimbabwe. He spent two months rehabilitating at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence (CoE) in Bengaluru, cleared the fitness tests, got some game time with the Dindigul Dragons in the Tamil Nadu Premier League in August, and returned with an encouraging performance on Sunday.

Speaking at the post-match press conference — before the injury was diagnosed — Chakaravarthy had reflected on the toll of constant rehabilitation. "Injuries are very common for all sportspeople, and it just shows that we are working, and we are giving our best. Sometimes, we push beyond our limits, and that's when the body gives in," he said. "So, that's when we have to take a step back and work better and come back stronger."

Centre of Excellence under the scanner

The latest setback has renewed questions about player fitness management at the CoE. It is not an isolated case: during the UK tour, pacer Harshit Rana suffered a hamstring injury, was sent back to India for rehab, and then suffered a rectus femoris strain during match simulation as part of his return-to-play process — with Yash Thakur named his replacement for the Afghanistan T20Is and Asian Games.

The Indian team management was reportedly taken aback by Chakaravarthy's latest injury, given that he had cleared his fitness test at the CoE before the series. The Indian Express understands he has been told to report to the CoE immediately for further tests.

What it means for the Asian Games

With the Indian team set to leave for the Asian Games in Japan on September 18, Chakaravarthy's availability remains unclear — a decision is expected only after the CoE medical team runs further tests. India still lead the three-match Afghanistan series 1-0, and their other spin options include Kuldeep Yadav, Krunal Pandya and uncapped Vipraj Nigam, with Bishnoi now in the XI.

For a spinner whose career has been defined by mystery variations and stop-start fitness, the next fortnight will decide whether the Asian Games campaign includes him at all.
